title: Semantic Layers for Reliable LLM-Powered Data Analytics: A Paired Benchmark of Accuracy and Hallucination Across Three Frontier Models
verified_fields: semantic layer = hand-authored markdown in prompt
notes: Single-shot, no tools/retries, medium reasoning effort. Table 1 (analytical verdict, n=99, q33 excluded for exceeding ClickHouse memory quota): Opus 4.7 50.5% [40.8, 60.1] -> 67.7% [58.0, 76.1] (+17.2); Sonnet 4.6 46.5% [37.0, 56.2] -> 68.7% [59.0, 77.0] (+22.2); GPT-5.4 45.5% [36.0, 55.2] -> 68.7% [59.0, 77.0] (+23.2). Brackets are Wilson 95% CIs. All three paired gains significant under two-sided exact McNemar, p <= 0.0015 (paper) / p < 0.002 (README). The 'semantic layer' is NOT a query engine: it is a markdown file describing measures, conventions and disambiguation rules, prepended to the prompt; the model still writes raw SQL. Primary metric is the 'analytical' judge verdict; 'strict' row match is secondary. Fetched 2026-09-30.

title: What Predicts Correctness in Text-to-SQL? A Selective-Prediction Study
notes: Summary: measures how well various signals predict whether generated SQL is correct (AUROC) on BIRD and Spider; black-box signals (self-consistency, schema relevance, executability) sit around 0.61-0.68, LLM judges reach 0.72-0.78, and a two-provider judge ensemble reaches 0.82 AUROC (ECE 0.03), enabling abstention frontiers such as answering 27% of questions at 24% selective risk. Relation: it frames correctness prediction for text-to-SQL as selective prediction (risk-coverage), the same accounting used to score trust labels and abstentions. Single-author preprint, not peer-reviewed. Fetched 2026-09-30.

title: Reliable Text-to-SQL with Adaptive Abstention
venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Management of Data (PACMMOD / SIGMOD) 3(1), pp. 1-30
notes: Summary: proposes RTS, which uses conformal prediction on LLM hidden states at the schema-linking step (Branching Point Prediction) to detect likely errors and either abstain or ask the user, giving probabilistic guarantees on schema-linking accuracy on BIRD. Relation: a system-level abstention mechanism for text-to-SQL, i.e. a 'stop instead of guess' policy whose value depends on how often it abstains versus answers wrongly. Author order differs: arXiv lists Chen, Chen, Yu, Koudas; the ACM/Crossref record lists Chen, Chen, Koudas, Yu (use the published order). The ACM article number could not be confirmed from a primary source. Fetched 2026-09-30.

title: Know What I don't Know: Handling Ambiguous and Unknown Questions for Text-to-SQL
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2023, pp. 5701-5714
notes: Summary: categorises ambiguous and unanswerable text-to-SQL questions into 6 feature categories, generates counterfactual ambiguous/unanswerable examples automatically, and proposes a weakly supervised Detecting-Then-Explaining (DTE) model to detect, localise and explain such errors. Relation: it treats 'this question should not get a SQL answer' as a first-class outcome, which is the case a correct refusal/stop label must capture. Fetched 2026-09-30.

title: Bluesky thread announcing arXiv penalty for unchecked LLM output
notes: Rule as posted: if there is incontrovertible evidence of LLM slop in a paper, the penalty is a 1-year ban from arXiv followed by a requirement that subsequent arXiv submissions must first be accepted at a reputable peer-reviewed venue. Examples of incontrovertible evidence: hallucinated references (not just minor errors) and LLM meta-comments left in the text. Later posts: co-authors should also be penalised (with appeal), and papers found this way are withdrawn. title: Submission guidelines / PDF submission guidelines
notes: Accepted formats in order of preference: (La)TeX / AMS(La)TeX / PDFLaTeX; PDF; HTML with JPEG/PNG/GIF images.
